submissions.findingTextShort: Dedicated scopoletin reviews describe predominantly experimental evidence and do not establish a standalone human clinical efficacy program.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 38464713 reviews scopoletin pharmacology, pharmacokinetics and toxicity and describes an evidence base dominated by in-vitro and in-vivo experimental work while calling for additional studies on toxicity, mechanisms and oral bioavailability. This is useful researched-null/translation-limit evidence, not a receipt for human treatment efficacy or a validated consumer regimen.
submissions.populationContext: Experimental scopoletin pharmacology and toxicology literature
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The finding records the directness of the reviewed evidence; it does not prove future human clinical evidence cannot emerge.

submissions.findingTextShort: Scopoletin is a hydroxycoumarin, so furanocoumarin-rich botanical photosensitivity and interaction language cannot transfer by broad family token overlap.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Scopoletin is 6-methoxy-7-hydroxycoumarin rather than a furanocoumarin. Safety inheritance must therefore follow exact chemical subclass and exposure provenance. Furanocoumarin-rich botanical or essential-oil photosensitivity, CYP and transporter hazards may remain related context where justified but cannot render as intrinsic scopoletin clinical risk without proposition-compatible evidence.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Structural distinction constrains inheritance; it does not assert absence of every possible scopoletin-specific interaction or adverse effect.

submissions.findingTextShort: Scopoletin experiments in IMR-90 human fibroblasts are human-derived cell evidence, not administered-human anti-aging efficacy.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 25837273 studied scopoletin in IMR-90 human lung fibroblast cells. Human cellular origin does not make the experiment a human participant intervention. The work may support mechanistic/autophagy context but cannot establish clinical anti-aging effects, participant safety, or an oral dose.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Mechanistic relevance may be retained without upgrading the evidence class to human clinical evidence.

submissions.findingTextShort: Dog pharmacokinetic/bioavailability data cannot establish human scopoletin bioavailability, safety, or consumer dosing.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 30421792 reports scopoletin pharmacokinetic/bioavailability work in dogs. Animal disposition may inform experimental translation but cannot satisfy human pharmacokinetic, safety-incidence, or consumer-dose gates. Species identity must survive normalization rather than being converted into a generic oral regimen.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Animal PK can motivate human study design but is not a human regimen receipt.

submissions.findingTextShort: Scoparone metabolism to scopoletin is a directional metabolic relationship, not synonymy or therapeutic evidence interchangeability.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Scoparone metabolism literature includes conversion pathways involving scopoletin and related metabolites, including human liver-microsome experiments. Precursor-to-metabolite relationship is directional and does not make scoparone administration an isolated-scopoletin intervention. Human microsomes also remain an in-vitro system rather than human participant evidence.
submissions.populationContext: Metabolic pathway and human liver-microsome context
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Metabolic relatedness supports graph edges, not alias equivalence or automatic efficacy transfer.
